issues.title: Neural-operator sensor subscript
issues.failure_explanation: In the old formula, the inner sum equals x(s_j) times the sum of the l-indexed weights, so it does not form a linear combination of values at distinct sensors. Consequently the executable construction cannot represent the multi-sensor branch input used by the universal operator-approximation argument.
issues.overall_effect: The printed neural operator and training equation have a reduced additive single-sensor architecture, leaving the cited universal operator and mollified L^2 approximation results unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace x(s_j) by x(s_l) inside every l-indexed branch sum in eq:deeponet and eq:learn, and index the corresponding sensor declaration by l. Read th:operatorapx and th:l2 operator apx with this multisensor architecture; their statements and proofs otherwise remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The l-indexed weights, sensor count N_l, and the later formula eq:nldeep using x(s_l) uniquely force this correction. The reasoning uses the standard multisensor architecture rather than the literal additive single-sensor formula, so this is a copied transcriptional subscript error.

issues.title: Projection bound omits the input norm
issues.failure_explanation: The old estimate replaces the action of the bounded operator (I-P_N)F on x by its operator norm alone. Since x ranges over a ball about xdag rather than the unit ball, the valid estimate is nu_N||x||, with ||x|| bounded by ||xdag|| plus the ball radius.
issues.overall_effect: The literal nonasymptotic error bound in the corollary is false. Its later big-O rate is not worsened because the omitted norm is uniformly bounded on the fixed local ball.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In eq:estimate use ‖(I−P_N)Fx‖ ≤ ‖(I−P_N)F‖‖x‖ and, for x in the stated ball, bound ‖x‖ by ‖x†‖ plus the ball radius. Carry this fixed multiplicative constant into the resulting operator-approximation bound.
issues.why_classification: The old line incorrectly applies an operator norm as though x had unit norm. Inserting the standard factor and bounding it on the fixed local ball is a short, routine repair that changes only a constant, not the corollary's method or asymptotic rate. Because an inequality must be repaired, it is not merely a typo.

issues.title: Compactness definition omits membership of the limit
issues.failure_explanation: Under the literal old definition, (0,1) is 'compact' in R because every sequence has a subsequence converging somewhere in R, although the limit may be 0 or 1. This weakened condition is insufficient for the later uniform functional and operator approximation statements: for example, a continuous functional such as t mapped to 1/(1-t) on the nonclosed constant-function domain is unbounded and cannot be uniformly approximated by a finite bounded-sigmoid network.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's compactness hypotheses literally permit nonclosed relatively compact domains, invalidating the compact-domain invocations in the listed approximation results.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the limit membership in def:compact from an element of V to an element of U, or K in the revised notation, and read every listed compactness hypothesis as genuine compactness rather than relative compactness.
issues.why_classification: The standard meaning of compactness, the declaration U⊆V, and the cited compact-domain approximation theorems uniquely require the subsequential limit to lie in U. The symbol V is a transcriptional membership error; correcting it restores the intended standard hypothesis without changing any approximation argument.

issues.title: Sobolev-to-uniform topology transfer fails for functional and operator approximation

failure_location.quote: be a continuous functional with respect to the $(H^s(\Omega_\X),\norms{\cdot}_{H^s})$-topology

diagnostic_evidence.quote: be a continuous operator with respect to the $(H^s(\Omega_\X),\norms{\cdot}_{H^s})$-topology

issues.failure_explanation: The functional and operator approximation statements share the same invalid transfer: H^s-continuity of F on a domain compact in C(overline Ω_X) does not imply continuity for the C supremum topology required by the point-sampling approximation argument. Their common justification invokes the compact Sobolev embedding, which does not provide this missing continuity. Choose smooth high-frequency functions u_k tending uniformly to zero but mutually separated, and separated from zero, in H^s. On D={0,u_1,u_2,...}, the scalar functional f(0)=0, f(u_k)=1 is H^s-continuous but not C-continuous, although D is C-compact. For a continuous bounded sigmoid allowed by the theorem, such as the logistic sigmoid, every finite point-sampling functional is C-continuous; it cannot approximate f uniformly to arbitrary accuracy. The operator counterexample is the same construction lifted to G(u)=f(u)g, where g is a fixed smooth output profile with L² norm one. Its finite neural-operator approximants are continuous from the input supremum topology to L², so the same obstruction applies. This argument does not assume that every possible bounded sigmoid is continuous; one allowed continuous choice suffices to refute the unrestricted statements.
issues.overall_effect: Both approximation theorems include maps that their point-sampling architectures cannot uniformly approximate. The scalar and L²-valued examples are two manifestations of the same topology mismatch, rather than two independent mechanisms. The separate sensor-index, compactness-definition and mollification defects remain separate records.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require F to be continuous on its domain for the C(overline Ω_X) supremum topology in both the functional and operator statements, with codomain R and L²(Ω_Y), respectively, and retain genuine compactness of the input domain in that topology. Apply the appropriate compact-domain approximation argument with this corrected premise, retaining the same architecture and uniform error criterion. For the operator architecture, the separately recorded sensor-index typo I001 must also be corrected. The authors' v3 adopts C-based continuity in both results and obtains C-compactness from H^s-boundedness and weak closedness. That revision supports the common topology repair; it does not turn all H^s-continuous maps into C-continuous ones or resolve the independent mollification issues.
issues.why_classification: Requiring continuity in the weaker input topology is a substantive narrowing of the permitted map class: it excludes the explicit scalar counterexample and its operator-valued lifting. Nevertheless, this is one contained correction to the shared approximation premise, preserving recognizable functional and operator approximation guarantees without reconstructing their proof architecture. The combined record is moderate, with both affected results retained.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: be a continuous functional on the space $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$

issues.title: Mollification can leave the operator domain
issues.failure_explanation: From x in D(F) it does not follow that M_xi x lies in D(F). For a constrained domain not preserved by convolution, F[x_xi] is undefined, although it is used in the first comparison and in the neural approximation step. Likewise, membership of only the center x* does not make F[x] defined throughout the displayed ball.
issues.overall_effect: The old L^2 approximation theorem is not even well-defined for general operator domains allowed by its context.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require, for each center covered by the local theorem, a radius r and smoothing level ξ such that B_r(x*)⊆D(F) and M_ξ(B_r(x*))⊆D(F), and carry this admissible ball through every occurrence of F[x] and F[M_ξx].
issues.why_classification: General constrained L^2 domains need not contain such a ball or be preserved by convolution, so this is not a notation-only well-definedness edit. The added local domain-compatibility premise leaves the proof method and error conclusion intact where it holds, but removes a real class of operator domains. That is a limited, recognizable weakening achievable without new proof architecture.

issues.title: Mollification does not preserve an arbitrarily centered ball
issues.failure_explanation: The cited inequality ||M_xi x||<=||x|| controls distance from zero, not distance from x*. In general M_xi(B_r(x*)) is centered near M_xi x*, so it need not lie in B_r(x*). The proof therefore fails to show that all smoothed arguments remain in the neighborhood where its local assumptions are to be used.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish its claimed localization of the mollified input class.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let B_R(x*) be the neighborhood on which the local assumptions hold. Choose ξ so that ‖M_ξx*−x*‖<R/2 and use inputs from B_{R/2}(x*); then ‖M_ξx−x*‖≤‖M_ξ(x−x*)‖+‖M_ξx*−x*‖<R. Replace the false same-radius inclusion by this nested-ball inclusion.
issues.why_classification: This is a routine contraction and triangle-inequality correction, together with shrinking an existential local neighborhood. It preserves the same local approximation statement and guarantees with no meaningful loss or new lemma. The old inference is genuinely invalid, so the issue is minor rather than a typo.

issues.title: Global-every-center L2 approximation is not supported

failure_location.quote: For every $\epsilon > 0$, there exist $\xi > 0$ and a vector $\mathcal{T}_\n$

issues.failure_explanation: The statement has the order 'for every epsilon, there exist xi and T_n' followed by 'for every x*', so the same finite network must have error at most epsilon at every center. The proof instead starts with a fixed x* and can at most construct xi, a neighborhood, and a network depending on that center. For F equal to the identity on all of L^2, the stated quantifiers would force one bounded finite-sigmoid neural operator to approximate every L^2 input to fixed absolute accuracy, which is impossible. The proof therefore supports only a center-dependent local claim, not the stated global one.
issues.overall_effect: The old theorem's one-operator approximation over all centers is unproved and false on admissible unbounded or noncompact L^2 domains; the later L^2 application cannot use that global guarantee.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the global quantifier order by: for every center x* and every ε>0, there exist r=r(x*,ε), ξ=ξ(x*,ε), and network parameters T_n=T_n(x*,ε) giving the error bound on B_r(x*). State this center dependence explicitly and use the result only at the selected center in the L^2 application.
issues.why_classification: The literal order promises one finite bounded-sigmoid operator for all centers, which is already impossible for the identity on all of L^2. Making the network center-dependent surrenders the central one-operator global applicability guarantee, while retaining it would require a substantially compacted input regime or essentially new architecture. Thus every established resolution entails major mathematical loss or global reconstruction.
